record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Can the measure-rigidity results for unipotent flows be extended to the adelic setting?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 10 (L. Silberman). Extend the results on measure rigidity of unipotent ﬂows to the adelic setting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a global field (for instance $\mathbb{Q}$) and let $\mathbb{A}$ denote its ring of adeles. Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected semisimple algebraic group defined over $K$, and consider the adelic homogeneous space $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})/\mathbf{G}(K)$. For each place $v$ of $K$, let $U_v \subset \mathbf{G}(K_v)$ be a subgroup generated by one-parameter unipotent subgroups, and let $U$ be a subgroup of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})$ that is a product (restricted with respect to compact open unipotent subgroups at non-archimedean places) of such groups $U_v$.

Establish an adelic analogue of Ratner's measure-classification theorem in this setting: prove that every $U$-invariant ergodic probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})/\mathbf{G}(K)$ is the homogeneous (algebraic) measure supported on a closed orbit $H x$, where $H$ is a closed subgroup of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})$ containing $U$ such that $Hx$ carries an $H$-invariant probability measure. Equivalently, extend the orbit-closure and equidistribution conclusions for unipotent flows from the real Lie group setting to the adelic homogeneous space $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A})/\mathbf{G}(K)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The measure classification for unipotent flows was extended to the S-arithmetic (and hence essentially adelic) setting by Ratner and independently by Margulis–Tomanov in the 1990s, treating products of unipotent groups over local fields acting on S-arithmetic quotients. The linearization technique was likewise adapted to this context by Tomanov and by Gorodnik–Oh. These S-arithmetic/adelic measure-rigidity results are now standard tools in the area, so the problem as posed is regarded as solved.

status_evidence.title: Ratner's theorems - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizations to the setting of products of real and p-adic Lie groups were given by Ratner and by Margulis and Tomanov.
status_evidence.claim: Ratner's measure rigidity has been extended to S-arithmetic/adelic settings by Ratner and by Margulis–Tomanov.

status_evidence.title: Flows on S-arithmetic homogeneous spaces and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Ratner's measure classification result was generalized to this context by Ratner and by Margulis and Tomanov; the linearization techniques of Dani and Margulis were adapted to this context by Tomanov and by Gorodnik and Oh.
status_evidence.claim: S-arithmetic generalizations of Ratner's theorems are established.
